records.screen: FIRST RUN What this copy needs ToolsEnabled works on one computer on its own. Some of its screens read reports that a group of computers writes, and on a fresh install nothing has written one yet. Here is what is missing, what you can do about it, and what is already working. Running an agent on this computer YOU CAN DO THIS NOW ToolsEnabled does not contain the program that runs an agent. Codex does, and it is a separate install. Once it is on this computer and signed in, the agent page can start a session. Every run is written down here before it begins. winget install OpenAI.Codex in Windows Terminal. If you already have Node, "npm install -g @openai/codex" does the same thing. codex login in the same window, once the install finishes. Turn on "Run an agent session" in Settings, under Write. Every action that writes anything ships switched off. Open Settings Why the fleet graph, comms board, metrics and ledger are empty NOTHING TO TURN ON Those screens read a report written by an agent host, and this copy of ToolsEnabled does not include one. There is no setting that connects one and no command that installs one, so nothing you do will fill those screens today. They say so rather than showing numbers that are not yours. This is the honest state of the product, not a fault on your computer. If you saw this on another screen, this is what it meant: No local agent fleet host detected on this machine. To see what one of those screens looks like with data in it, turn its live source off in Settings, under Data and Sim. Each screen then shows a worked example, labelled as an example. Open Settings Sending a message to a coordinator YOU CAN DO THIS NOW The box on the first page has no place to type. Sending replies is switched off, and there is no coordinator on this computer to send one to. Turning the switch on is worth doing so the box is ready. It will stay quiet until an agent host reports here. Turn on "Coordinator replies" in Settings, under Write. Open Settings What already works here NO SETUP Every agent run started from this window is written down on this computer, signed, and listed on the first page. The fleet graph draws the organisation this copy declares, and each agent on it opens a page of its own. The permission level you chose during setup is what a session is built from, and it can be changed in Settings. All settings Back to the first page

records.screen: FIRST RUN What this copy needs ToolsEnabled works on one computer on its own. Some of its screens read reports that a group of computers writes, and on a fresh install nothing has written one yet. Here is what is missing, what you can do about it, and what is already working. Running an agent on this computer YOU CAN DO THIS NOW ToolsEnabled does not contain the program that runs an agent. Codex does, and it is a separate install. Once it is on this computer and signed in, the agent page can start a session. Every run is written down here before it begins. winget install OpenAI.Codex in Windows Terminal. If you already have Node, "npm install -g @openai/codex" does the same thing. codex login in the same window, once the install finishes. Turn on "Run an agent session" in Settings, under Write. Every action that writes anything ships switched off. Open Settings Why the fleet graph, comms board, metrics and ledger are empty NOTHING TO TURN ON Those screens read a report written by an agent host, and this copy of ToolsEnabled does not include one. There is no setting that connects one and no command that installs one, so nothing you do will fill those screens today. They say so rather than showing numbers that are not yours. This is the honest state of the product, not a fault on your computer. If you saw this on another screen, this is what it meant: No local agent fleet host detected on this machine. To see what one of those screens looks like with data in it, turn its live source off in Settings, under Data and Sim. Each screen then shows a worked example, labelled as an example. Open Settings Sending a message to a coordinator YOU CAN DO THIS NOW The box on the first page has no place to type. Sending replies is switched off, and there is no coordinator on this computer to send one to. Turning the switch on is worth doing so the box is ready. It will stay quiet until an agent host reports here. Turn on "Coordinator replies" in Settings, under Write. Open Settings What already works here NO SETUP Every agent run started from this window is written down on this computer, signed, and listed on the first page. The fleet graph draws the organisation this copy declares, and each agent on it opens a page of its own. The permission level you chose during setup is what a session is built from, and it can be changed in Settings. All settings Back to the first page

records.screen: Who is using this copy? SIGN IN SO THE RECORD OF WHAT YOUR ASSISTANT DOES SAYS WHO ASKED FOR IT. Sign in with Google — not available on this copy This copy has not been given a Google sign-in application id yet, so signing in with Google is not available. Making an account on this computer works now and does the same job. Sign in with Google USE AN ACCOUNT ON THIS COMPUTER. Name Letters, numbers, and . _ - between them. This is what the record of your assistant’s work will name. Shown as Optional. How the program greets you. Leave it blank to be greeted by the name above. Password At least 12 characters. Length is what makes a password hard to guess — a few unrelated words beat a short one with symbols in it. There is no reset, so use your password manager. What this account is, before you make one. It is an account on this computer. Nothing is sent anywhere, no email address is asked for, and no server holds it — so there is also no password reset. If you forget it, the account cannot be recovered and you make a new one. Signing in with Google instead puts the verified email address from your Google account on the record. Google is what checks it, not this computer. Either way it is not a login to Claude or ChatGPT, and it does not carry a subscription. Those stay in their own programs; this one only answers who is using this copy. It records who asked for a piece of work. It is not a lock on this computer: anyone already signed in to Windows as you can remove it.
